reading_rule: Consume each row as a premise or falsifier before proof search. A result implied by a row is dominated; use the stronger row and continue toward the parent theorem. Route choice remains unrestricted.

results.exact_statement: For every integer t >= -1 let S_t = sum_{n>=2} 1/(n! + t) and C_t = sum_{n>=2} 1/(n!(n! + t)). Lean proves the termwise identity 1/(n! + t) = 1/n! - t/(n!(n! + t)), summability of both series, the decomposition S_t = (-t C_t) + (e - 2), and hence: S_t is rational iff ceil(t m! C_t) = 2 (mod m) for all sufficiently large m, and irrational iff that ceiling escapes residue 2 cofinally. The member t = -1 is kernel-identified with the Erdos #68 series, where the condition is floor(m! C) = -2 (mod m); the member t = 0 is kernel-identified with e - 2, whose orbit ceil(0) = 0 never lies in residue class 2 for m >= 3, so the boundary REPROVES that e is irrational. This places Erdos's whole conjectured family (Erdos 1988, p. 102) under one explicit companion-orbit boundary extending Cantor's factorial-base criterion. It decides no member with t != 0.
results.hypotheses: Lean-checked family equivalence, fifteen named declarations, lean_fast_build exit 0 on 2026-09-02. Finite evidence: residue-2 hits for t = 1,2,3,5 through m = 400 are consistent with a 1/m hit rate.
supersedes: the single-member companion-orbit boundary for t = -1 alone
Cantor's factorial-base criterion in its unparameterised form
results.why_it_matters: One criterion covers Erdos's entire conjectured family and specialises to a proof that e is irrational. That is a clean, legible theorem an outside number theorist can check in an afternoon, and it is currently uncommitted to any public entry beyond the t = -1 member.

results.exact_statement: S not in Q if and only if for every B there is m > B with factorialGapScaledTail m <= m r_(m-1), that is, cofinal escape from the lower endpoint cylinder. Since 0 < factorialGapScaledTail m < 2/m, the trapping radius is O(m^-2). The escape criterion is exactly the harmless-carry criterion (factorialGap_lower_endpoint_escape_iff_nonunit_or_maximal_digit), it is strictly more permissive than the carry target, and it admits a tail-free two-sided consumer over the finite predecessor gap.
results.hypotheses: Lean-checked normal form. It produces no cofinal escape events; #68 remains open.
supersedes: the cofinal non-unit carry normal form
the cofinal strict-successor divisibility miss normal form
results.why_it_matters: It is the corpus's own statement that Erdos #68 is an explicit deterministic shrinking-target problem with a quadratically small target. Four sibling problems have the same shape and nobody has written the dictionary.

results.exact_statement: With C = sum_{n>=2} 1/(n!(n! - 1)), F_m = m! C_m, delta_m = m! sum_{n>m} 1/(n!(n! - 1)) and sigma_m = [fract(m!C) < delta_m], Lean proves F_m = m! C - delta_m with 0 < delta_m < 1/((m+1)! - 1) for m >= 2, the wrap identity floor(F_m) = floor(m!C) - sigma_m, and for every m >= 3 the exact carry law b_m = (m - 1 - d_m(C)) + sigma_m - m sigma_(m-1). Consequences: a unit carry forces d_m(C) in {m-2, m-1}; a zero carry forces d_m(C) in {m-1, 0}; if floor(m!C) avoids both residues -2 and -1 mod m then b_m != 1. The exact probe finds no wrap through m = 160, smallest fract(m!C)/delta_m ratio 18.7.
results.hypotheses: Lean-checked exact identity, thirteen named declarations. It produces no cofinal miss and no irrationality claim.
results.why_it_matters: It makes the whole #68 carry sequence an exact function of one real constant plus a sub-factorial exceptional indicator.

results.exact_statement: The shift-family companion-orbit boundary decides no member with t != 0. Residue-2 hits for t = 1, 2, 3, 5 through m = 400 are [3,30,110], [3,13,61,227,377], [6,31,45,56], [11,14,20,28,29,309], consistent with a 1/m hit rate, so finite hit tables are not evidence in either direction.

results.why_it_matters: A finite scan of the residue orbit cannot decide any member; only a cofinal miss theorem can.

results.exact_statement: The exact GMP computation of every strict-successor carry for 3 <= m <= 300000 gives only q >= 300000 for a rational S = a/q. The only unit carries are m = 52, 591, 1030, 1407, 1438, 2164, 4258, 10991, 21236. Correctly indexed arithmetic shows prime failures at m = 5 and m = 23, so the universal all-primes shortcut is FALSE.
results.hypotheses: Exact integer computation at 5025679 bits with 96 guard bits, no floating point.
results.why_it_matters: A finite horizon never discharges a cofinal quantifier, and the obvious prime shortcut is already refuted at m = 5 and m = 23.
